mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stays below its recent 4-week average, weekday trip chaining into shopping districts remains weak and RETAIL_REC will drift lower over the next four weeks. This mechanism is falsified if a further drop in WORKPLACES does not coincide with weaker retail mobility.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not lower than over the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES remaining below -30 for the period.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in TRANSIT from the current low level should raise retail access within one to two weeks because more passengers pass through commercial corridors before and after travel. The signal fails if transit rises without any accompanying lift in retail mobility.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises at least 3 points week-on-week from a base below -35
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days after TRANSIT rises from below -35, or retail remains flat while transit increases.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility rises while PARKS collapses, households are staying local and substituting toward neighborhood errands, which lifts retail-and-recreation visits over the next four weeks. The mechanism is rejected if high home-stay does not translate into more local retail activity.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days when RESIDENTIAL stays above 10 and PARKS stays below -10.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both drop sharply in the same week, the city is likely in a tightening or disruption regime that suppresses discretionary shopping trips, pushing RETAIL_REC down over the following four weeks. The claim fails when simultaneous commuting weakness does not precede retail weakness.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES each fall below their prior week by at least 2 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 28 days after a week in which both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES each fall by 2 or more points.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp weekly jump in PARKS during warm-weather or leisure periods pulls visits toward outdoor recreation and away from indoor retail, reducing RETAIL_REC within one week and keeping it softer for up to two weeks. The effect fails if park surges do not coincide with retail softness.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower in the next 7 to 14 days after PARKS jumps by more than 10 points.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM remains less negative than RETAIL_REC, essential-shopping trips are holding up better than discretionary trips, implying substitution away from retail-and-recreation and a further decline in RETAIL_REC over four weeks. The mechanism fails if essentials weaken more than retail or if the gap closes without retail falling.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 28 days while GROCERY_PHARM remains at least 20 points above RETAIL_REC.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stops falling and turns upward after several depressed weeks, the commuting base is rebuilding and retail mobility should improve with a two-week lag as lunchtime and after-work shopping returns. The signal is rejected if workplace recovery does not lead retail recovery.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises after at least two consecutive weeks below -32
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days after WORKPLACES rises following two weeks below -32.

mechanism_narrative: In a mobility-restriction regime, a simultaneous decline in TRANSIT and rise in RESIDENTIAL signals containment behavior that suppresses discretionary outings, so RETAIL_REC should move lower over the next four weeks. The claim is falsified if retail does not weaken under this mixed movement pattern.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower over the next 28 days when TRANSIT remains below -38 and RESIDENTIAL stays above 10.
